# Two node props that read each other have no answer, and the checker says
# so with a position, naming each read on the way round.
#
# A prop read off a `#id` whose node the target keeps nothing of is answered
# with the expression the prop was given, and answering runs to a fixed point
# because one answer can uncover the next -- `circle #b(r=a.r)` is a read that
# only becomes readable once `a`'s own props are known. A cycle has no fixed
# point to reach. The lowering used to be what found it (passNodePropReads,
# which keeps the check for IR the checker did not see); the read graph is
# known when the program is checked, so the question is asked there.

! sngl check .
stderr 'app.sngl:6:42: a cycle: a.r reads b.r, b.r reads a.r; each needs the next one''s value first, so none has one'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import draw "sngl:ui/draw"

ui.window #w(title="t") {
    draw.canvas(width=10px, height=10px) {
        draw.circle #a(cx=1.0, cy=1.0, r=b.r)
        draw.circle #b(cx=2.0, cy=2.0, r=a.r)
    }

    ui.text(value="a is {a.r}")
}
